# whoiskawhan.com

> whoiskawhan.com is the personal editorial website of Kawhan Laurindo, a Brazilian fullstack software engineer. The site combines technical writing, short learning notes, portfolio material, open source projects, books, hobbies, and professional background. Primary languages are pt-BR and English.

This file is intended to help LLMs and agents understand the public structure of the site quickly.

Important notes:

- The site is content-first and editorial in tone, not a SaaS product or API platform.
- Most core pages are available in pt-BR and under `/en/` in English.
- Blog posts and TIL notes are localized in pt-BR and English when translations exist.
- Every page is prerendered to static HTML, so content is readable without running JavaScript.
- There are no public markdown mirrors of pages yet; use the curated links below or the sitemap.

## Primary pages

- [Home](https://whoiskawhan.com/): Site entry point with author positioning, recent writing, and open source highlights.
- [About](https://whoiskawhan.com/about): Biography, career timeline, technical background, and side project context.
- [Certificates](https://whoiskawhan.com/certificates): Professional certifications and verified badges.
- [Portfolio](https://whoiskawhan.com/portfolio): Main areas of work, including payments, frontend systems, and runtime/operations, plus open source projects.
- [Blog](https://whoiskawhan.com/blog): Long-form technical writing about software architecture, frontend, operations, payments, and engineering decisions.
- [TIL](https://whoiskawhan.com/til): Short learning notes and technical observations.
- [Books](https://whoiskawhan.com/books): Curated engineering and adjacent reading recommendations.
- [Hobbies](https://whoiskawhan.com/hobbies): Personal interests outside engineering (games, manga, anime, tabletop RPG) and Pocket Kawhan, a playable handheld console with seven small browser games built from scratch for the site.

## Project pages

Each open source project has a detail page with overview, concept, features, stack, and links to the repository. English versions live under `/en/projects/`.

- [Sales Project](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/salesProject): .NET sales API with DDD, CQRS via MediatR, and domain events published to RabbitMQ.
- [Good Hamburger](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/goodHamburger): .NET ordering API for a burger joint that detects combos and applies the best discount; EF Core, PostgreSQL, tested rules.
- [Opportunity Microservices](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/springMicroservices): Opportunity split into Spring Boot microservices with Eureka discovery and an authenticating gateway.
- [Opportunity](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/opportunity): Job board for UFPB Campus IV with institutional sign-in and interest charts; Django, PostgreSQL, JWT, Docker.
- [libft](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/libft): Reimplementation of the C standard library, built at 42 São Paulo.
- [NLW Journey API](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/journeyApi): .NET API written with DDD, Entity Framework, FluentValidation, and Swagger.
- [Pokédex Angular](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/pokedexAngular): Angular Pokédex backed by the PokéAPI, organized by domain.
- [Controle de Contatos](https://whoiskawhan.com/projects/controleContatos): ASP.NET MVC CRUD with authentication, per-level permissions, and SMTP password recovery.

## Content and interpretation guidance

- The author writes in an editorial, direct, anti-corporate tone focused on real-world software engineering.
- Topics commonly include architecture, frontend systems, APIs, payments, DevOps, operational reliability, and open source.
- The portfolio describes professional areas of expertise and delivery; individual open source projects are detailed on the project pages above.
- The site is personal but professionally relevant: useful for understanding the author's background, interests, writing, and technical positioning.
- For current updates, prefer the homepage, blog index, and about page.
